title: Seismic Refraction — Layer Depth (Two-Layer Case)

x_c.description: Crossover distance (where refracted arrival overtakes direct arrival)

applicability: Simple two-layer case. Requires V₂ > V₁. For multi-layer cases, use generalized reciprocal method (GRM) or tomographic inversion. Also: z₁ = (ti × V₁ × V₂) / (2 × √(V₂² - V₁²)) where ti = intercept time.

title: Rayleigh Wave Depth of Investigation

V_R.description: Rayleigh wave phase velocity at minimum frequency

f_min.description: Minimum usable frequency in dispersion curve

applicability: MASW depth depends on lowest frequency with reliable phase velocity. Active source: f_min ≈ 4–8 Hz. Passive source can reach 1–3 Hz for deeper investigation. Vs ≈ 1.1 × V_R (Rayleigh wave velocity is ~90% of shear wave velocity).
source: Park et al. (1999), Xia et al. (1999)

title: Vs30 — Time-Averaged Shear Wave Velocity
equation: Vs30 = 30 / Σ(di / Vsi)  for i = 1 to n layers within 30 m

Vs30.description: Time-averaged shear wave velocity in upper 30 m

Vsi.description: Shear wave velocity of layer i

applicability: Used for IBC/ASCE 7 seismic site classification: Site Class A (Vs30 > 1500), B (760–1500), C (360–760), D (180–360), E (< 180 m/s). MASW is the most common field method for Vs30 determination.

title: Apparent Resistivity — Wenner Array

ΔV.description: Measured potential difference between inner electrodes

applicability: Wenner array: equal spacing, good vertical resolution. Depth of investigation ≈ 0.5a (median depth of sensitivity). For other arrays, geometric factor K differs: Schlumberger K = π×n×(n+1)×a, dipole-dipole K = π×n×(n+1)×(n+2)×a.

title: GPR Depth of Penetration
applicability: GPR velocity: v = c/√ε_r. Typical ε_r: dry sand 3–5, wet sand 20–30, clay 5–40, water 80, air 1, concrete 6–11. Resolution ≈ λ/4 = v/(4f). Example: 400 MHz in dry sand (v≈0.15 m/ns) → resolution ≈ 0.09 m.

title: Electromagnetic Skin Depth

δ.description: Skin depth — depth at which EM signal attenuates to 1/e (37%)

applicability: Lower frequency → deeper penetration. Higher resistivity → deeper penetration. EM31 at ~9.8 kHz in 100 Ω·m ground: δ ≈ 50 m, effective exploration depth ≈ 1.5δ for vertical dipole. Conductive ground (10 Ω·m) reduces depth dramatically.

title: Seismic Rippability Index (from Refraction Velocity)
equation: Rippability assessment based on Vp threshold
applicability: Caterpillar rippability chart (D8/D9/D10 dozers): Generally rippable if Vp < 1500–2000 m/s. Marginal 2000–2500 m/s. Non-rippable > 2500–3000 m/s (varies by rock type and dozer class). Correlations are equipment-specific — use manufacturer charts.

title: Gravity Anomaly from Spherical Void
equation: Δg_max = (4/3) × π × G × Δρ × R³ / z²

Δg_max.description: Maximum gravity anomaly directly above void

Δρ.description: Density contrast (host rock - void fill; ≈ -2000 to -2500 kg/m³ for air-filled void in rock)

applicability: Detectable anomaly depends on instrument precision (~1–5 μGal for modern instruments) and noise. Example: 3 m radius void at 10 m depth in limestone (Δρ ≈ -2400): Δg ≈ -0.006 mGal = -6 μGal — marginally detectable. Deeper or smaller voids may not be resolvable.
